title: AI Hallucinations in State Farm Insurance Outside Lawyers' Filings

reading.body:
The failure here is a well-documented one: a generative AI tool produced plausible-looking but entirely fictitious legal citations, and those citations entered court filings without verification. Seven nonexistent cases appeared across eight filings, accompanied by fabricated quotes and holdings. The error occurred at the point where a lawyer relied on the AI tool, Irys, under the mistaken belief that it would itself check the accuracy of citations, a belief that proved incorrect.

This is a model asserting fabricated content as fact, the classic hallucination failure mode, combined with a deployment that lacked any human verification step before the output reached an official legal document. The citations would have been catchable by checking each one against an authoritative legal database before filing, a step that was not taken. The mistake was discovered not by the filing lawyers but by opposing counsel.

What is not established is whether Irys was designed or marketed as a citation-verification tool, or whether the lawyer's belief about its capabilities was a misreading of its intended function.

reports.title: State Farm defense lawyers admit AI generated fake cases in LA lawsuit
AI hallucinated case law in insurance company’s filings in L.A. County house fire dispute
AI Hallucinations in State Farm Insurance Outside Lawyers' Filings

summary:
# Summary

State Farm's defense lawyers apologized for using artificial intelligence that generated fake legal cases in their filings for a lawsuit brought by Los Angeles homeowner Fa'alagilagi Meni-Siliga. The plaintiff's attorneys discovered that State Farm's motions contained seven nonexistent case citations across eight filings, along with fake quotes and holdings. Lawyer Jacquelene Robinson admitted she used an AI tool called Irys, which she mistakenly believed would perform accuracy checks on legal citations. The case involves Meni-Siliga's home in Carson, which became uninhabitable after a 2020 fire, with subsequent water damage during repairs. She claims State Farm delayed approving repairs, leaving her home incomplete and forcing her family into bankruptcy and foreclosure. The trial is scheduled for October.

The incident highlights growing concerns about artificial intelligence in the legal profession, with 41 percent of law firms now using generative AI. A database tracking legal hallucinations worldwide has documented 1,922 cases, mostly in the United States. Last year, a California attorney received a record ten thousand dollar fine for submitting a brief with twenty-one fabricated quotes. State Farm stated it expects its external legal counsel to maintain the highest ethical standards and verify all filings' accuracy.
